title: Karl Holzer (Director of People & Operations, Sclable) reads financial gravity through Luhmann — 'Eine Mission, die nur in der Kultur lebt, bleibt aber im Reden'
summary: A German-language essay answering the line every founder hears: we trust our culture, extra structure only slows us down. Holzer uses Luhmann's distinction between decidable and non-decidable decision premises to argue culture is the part an organisation can least control, then takes up the book's financial gravity: it wins conflicts because it is written down — budgets, targets, the shareholder agreement. He reads Patagonia not as a counter-example but as proof, since Chouinard moved the mission into a trust rather than trusting culture to outlive him.
blockquote: Eine Mission, die nur in der Kultur lebt, bleibt aber im Reden. Satzung, Stimmrechte, etc. holen sie ins Entscheiden. Dort kann sie dann auch gegen ein Budget antreten.
attribution_title: Director of People & Operations, Sclable · Organizational development

type_metadata.translation: A mission that lives only in the culture stays in the talking. Bylaws, voting rights and the rest bring it into deciding. There it can hold its own against a budget.
